title: Validate recovery chain base compatibility by edge
rawUserRequest: Continue the deep performance Work Item, and fix discovered process problems durably before proceeding.

declaredIntent.summary: Validate the recovery-chain root against the PR base and each later recovery against only its immediate predecessor.

outOfScope: Weakening any source reference, approval, receipt, sequence, or ancestry predicate
General performance implementation, WI-10 installation changes, or release publication

sources.reason: The immediate predecessor completes the fourth archive in the rejected recovery chain.
The aggregate PR gate currently applies root PR-base compatibility to every recovery edge.
The existing chain test mocks all ancestry checks successful and cannot detect reverse PR-base compatibility.

riskAssessment.reason: Incorrect base semantics can either reject a valid immutable recovery chain or accidentally weaken Work Item ownership.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized continuous process-first correction.

preReviewWarnings: Verify only the chain root consumes PR-base compatibility and every later edge retains direct ancestry plus all existing recovery predicates.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The recovery-chain root must be compatible with the PR merge-base.
Each later recovery must be a descendant of its immediate predecessor base without being required to be an ancestor of the PR base.
A precise ancestry graph regression fails the old implementation and passes the corrected implementation.
Broken ancestry, source reference, approval, receipt, or sequence still rejects the entire chain.
RFE-ISSUE-142 and traceability record the real aggregate failure, mock gap, fix, and complete lifecycle.
Full quality, aggregate five-item PR validation, hosted CI, merge, closure, cleanup, and synchronization complete before performance resumes.
guidelines: Separate root PR-base validation from pairwise chain-edge validation.
Use a realistic directed ancestry graph in tests; do not mock all Git relations as true.
Preserve every existing fail-closed recovery predicate and unrelated bundle rejection.

intent.problem: The generalized chain reused a pair predicate that requires each predecessor base to be compatible with the original PR merge-base. Valid later recoveries point forward from the PR base and therefore fail. The unit test returned success for every Git ancestry query, hiding this reverse relation.
constraints: Only the first archive may consume PR merge-base compatibility.
Every later edge must retain direct predecessor-to-recovery ancestry and all non-ancestry predicates.
Use the real five-archive branch as aggregate acceptance evidence.
intent.rationale: A chain has one root relation to the PR and N-1 edge relations. Modeling them separately matches Git directionality and keeps unrelated bundles fail closed.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The root base is PR-compatible and later bases form only forward adjacent ancestry.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The complete recovery chain is accepted.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use a directed fake ancestry graph and run the real aggregate PR gate.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A later edge is broken or the root is not PR-compatible.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user requires discovered process defects to be fixed before performance resumes.
